paragraphs: Compass Diversified Holdings, a Delaware statutory trust, was formed in Delaware on November 18, 2005. Compass Group Diversified Holdings, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, was also formed on November 18, 2005. The Trust and the LLC were formed to acquire and manage a group of small and middle-market businesses headquartered in North America. The Trust is the sole owner of 100% of the Trust Interests, as defined in our LLC Agreement, of the LLC. Pursuant to the LLC Agreement, the Trust owns an identical number of Trust Interests in the LLC as exist for the number of outstanding shares of the Trust.
The Trust was previously treated as a partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes but elected, effective September 1, 2021, to be taxed as an association taxable as a corporation.

The LLC is the operating entity with a board of directors (the "Board") whose corporate governance responsibilities are similar to that of a Delaware corporation. The LLC's Board oversees the management of the Company and our businesses and the performance of our Manager. Certain persons who are employees, former employees or members of our Manager receive a profit allocation as beneficial owners (through Sostratus LLC) of the Allocation Interests, as defined in our LLC Agreement.

We acquire controlling interests in and actively manage our subsidiaries that we believe (i) operate in industries with long-term macroeconomic growth opportunities, (ii) have positive and stable cash flows, (iii) face minimal threats of technological or competitive obsolescence, and (iv) have strong management teams largely in place. We offer investors a unique opportunity to own a diverse group of leading middle-market businesses in the branded-consumer and industrial sectors.

Our disciplined approach to our target markets provides opportunities to methodically acquire and manage attractive businesses that will create value for our shareholders. For sellers of businesses, our unique financial structure allows us to purchase businesses efficiently with fewer third-party financing contingencies and, following acquisition, to provide our businesses with access to growth capital. In addition, our permanent capital model generally allows us to acquire businesses at any point across economic cycles, ensuring that we are able to act quickly when the opportunity presents itself, even when markets are volatile.
Private company operators and corporate parents looking to sell their business units may consider us an attractive purchaser because of our ability to:
•provide ongoing strategic and financial support for their businesses, including professionalization of our subsidiaries at scale;
•maintain a long-term outlook as to the ownership of those businesses; •sustainably invest in growth capital and/or add-on acquisitions where appropriate; and
•consummate transactions efficiently without being dependent on third-party transaction financing.

In particular, our long-term approach and our active management may alleviate the concern that many private company operators and parent companies may have with regard to their businesses going through multiple sale processes in a short period of time. We believe our approach enhances our ability to develop a comprehensive strategy to grow the earnings and cash flows of each of our businesses.

Finally, it has been our experience, that our ability to acquire businesses without the cumbersome delays and conditions typical of third-party transactional financing is appealing to sellers of businesses who are interested in confidentiality, speed and certainty of close.

Our management team's strong relationships with industry executives, accountants, attorneys, business brokers, commercial and investment bankers, and other potential sources of acquisition opportunities offer us opportunities to assess small to middle market businesses available for acquisition. In addition, the flexibility, creativity, experience and expertise of our management team in structuring transactions allows us to consider non-traditional and complex transactions tailored to fit a specific acquisition target.

We categorize the current businesses we own into two separate groups: (i) branded consumer businesses and (ii) industrial businesses. Branded consumer businesses are those businesses that we believe capitalize on a valuable brand name in their respective market sector. We believe that our branded consumer businesses are leaders in their product categories. Industrial businesses are those businesses that focus on manufacturing and selling products and/or industrial services within a specific market sector. We believe that our industrial businesses are leaders in their specific market sectors.

headings: Risk Factors Relating to the Lugano Investigation and Restatements
Our intercompany loan to Lugano is subject to risk of loss.
We are subject to ongoing government investigations relating to the Lugano matters, and such investigations could result in enforcement actions, penalties, and additional costs.
Risks Related to Our Business and Structure

The success of our branded consumer businesses depends on our ability to maintain the value and reputation of the brand and the failure to do so could reduce profits and adversely impact our financial condition.

Under the Trust Agreement, the Company's Board will have the power to cause the Trust to be converted to a corporation in the future at its sole discretion in ways with which our shareholders may disagree.
We rely entirely on receipts from our businesses to make distributions to our shareholders.
The Company's Board has the power to change the terms of our shares in its sole discretion in ways with which you may disagree.
We may have conflicts of interest with the noncontrolling shareholders of our businesses.

Our substantial indebtedness and exposure to variable interest rates could materially adversely affect our liquidity, financial condition, and ability to operate our business, service our debt, and make distributions.
We may engage in a business transaction with one or more target businesses that have relationships with our officers, our directors, or our Manager, which may create potential conflicts of interest.
Changes to U.S. tariff and import/export regulations may have a negative effect on economic activity, financial conditions and results of our businesses.
Risks Related to Taxation

Future changes to tax laws are uncertain and may result in the Trust paying corporate income tax at rates higher than expected or result in the Trust failing to realize the anticipated benefits of the Election.
Risks Related to the Preferred Shares
Distributions on the Series A Preferred Shares are discretionary and non-cumulative.
The Series A, Series B and Series C Preferred Shares are equity securities and are subordinated to our existing and future indebtedness.
Risks Relating to Our Manager
Our Manager and its affiliates, including members of our management team, may engage in activities that compete with us or our businesses.
We cannot remove our Manager solely for poor performance, which could limit our ability to improve our performance and could materially adversely affect the market price of our shares.
We must pay our Manager the base management fee regardless of our performance.
We cannot determine the amount of profit allocation that will be paid over time with any certainty.
Our profit allocation may induce our Manager to make suboptimal decisions regarding our operations.
The obligations to pay management fees and profit allocation may cause the Company to liquidate assets or incur debt.

paragraphs: Our business, operations and financial condition are subject to various risks and uncertainties. The following discussion of risk factors should be read in conjunction with the Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations set forth in Part II, Item. 7 and the "Consolidated Financial Statements" and related notes of this Form 10-K. If any of these risks actually occur, our business, financial condition, operating results and prospects could be materially and adversely affected. In addition to the factors affecting our specific operating segments identified in connection with the descriptions of these segments and the financial results of the operations of these operating segments elsewhere in this report, the following discussion sets forth the material risk factors we face which make an investment in us speculative or risky.

We have restated certain of our prior consolidated financial statements as a result of the Lugano Investigation, which resulted in unanticipated costs, litigation against Lugano and the Company and stockholder litigation against the Company, and may result in additional stockholder litigation, regulatory consequences and additional liabilities we are currently unaware of, and may adversely affect investor confidence, our stock price, our ability to raise capital in the future, and our reputation.

As previously disclosed, following concerns reported to the Company's management, the Company commenced the Lugano Investigation. As a result of the Lugano Investigation, the Company determined that the Company's previously issued financial statements for fiscal years 2022, 2023, 2024, and the first three fiscal quarters of 2025 including other interim and full-year financial information should no longer be relied upon. The Company corrected these errors in its 2024 Form 10K/A which was filed on December 8, 2025, and its Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q for the first, second, and third quarters of 2025, which were filed on December 18, 2025, December 29, 2025 and January 14, 2026 respectively.

We have incurred unanticipated costs for accounting, financing and legal fees in connection with the Lugano Investigation and the restatements, including those associated with our entry into forbearance agreements, amendments, and waivers with respect to our Credit Agreement and senior note indentures due to potential defaults or events of default thereunder. The restatements may erode investor confidence in our Company, our financial reporting, accounting practices and processes, and may raise reputational issues for our business. The Lugano Investigation and the restatement of our historical financial statements have negatively impacted, and may continue to negatively impact, the trading price of our securities, have made it more difficult for us to comply with our debt covenants and tightened our liquidity, and may make it more difficult for us to raise capital on acceptable terms, or at all, in the future. In light of the Lugano Investigation and related matters, we have taken certain actions to preserve liquidity, including suspending distributions on our common shares, and our ability to access the equity capital markets, including through at-the-market equity offerings, was limited during 2025 in light of the Lugano Investigation and related events.

In addition, the Lugano Investigation, the restatements and related material weaknesses in our internal control over financial reporting have resulted in litigation against Lugano and the Company, and stockholder litigation against the Company, and regulatory investigations and inquiries which may result in adverse regulatory consequences. As previously disclosed, there are ongoing investigations initiated by the SEC and the U.S. Department of Justice ("DOJ"), and FINRA conducted a review of trading activity in our securities and referred the matter to the SEC for whatever actions the SEC deemed appropriate, if any. These and any future regulatory consequences, litigation, claims or disputes, whether successful or not, could subject us to additional costs or liabilities we are currently unaware of, divert the attention of our management, or impair our reputation. Each of these consequences could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition.

We have identified material weaknesses in our internal control over financial reporting, which could, if not properly remediated, result in additional material misstatements in our interim or annual consolidated financial statements, impact the Company's ability to report its results of operations and financial condition accurately and in a timely manner. If we are unable to remediate these material weaknesses, or if we identify additional material weaknesses in the future or otherwise fail to maintain effective internal control over financial reporting or disclosure controls and procedures, it could result in future material misstatements of our consolidated financial statements or could cause us to fail to meet our periodic reporting obligations, which may adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, investor confidence in our business, or the trading price of our securities.

Compass Diversified Holdings, a Delaware statutory trust, was formed in Delaware on November 18, 2005. Compass Group Diversified Holdings LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, was also formed on November 18, 2005. In accordance with the Trust Agreement, the Trust is the sole owner of 100% of the Trust Interests (as defined in the LLC Agreement of the Company). Pursuant to the LLC Agreement, the Company has outstanding an identical number of Trust Interests as the number of outstanding shares of the Trust. Sostratus LLC owns all of our Allocation Interests. The Company is the operating entity with a board of directors and corporate governance responsibilities similar to those of a Delaware corporation.

The Trust and the LLC were formed to acquire and manage a group of small and middle-market businesses headquartered in North America. We characterize small and middle market businesses as those that generate annual cash flows of up to $100 million. We focus on companies of this size because we believe they are better able to achieve growth rates above those of their relevant industries and efforts to improve earnings and cash flow are often more effective in companies of this size. In pursuing new acquisitions, we seek businesses with the following characteristics:
•North American base of operations; •Stable and growing earnings and cashflow; •Significant market share in defensible industry niches (i.e., has a "reason to exist");
•Solid and proven management team with meaningful incentives; •Low technological and/or product obsolescence risk; and
•Diversified customer and supplier bases.
Our management team's strategy for our subsidiaries involves:
•Utilizing structured incentive compensation programs tailored to each business to attract and retain talented managers;
•Assisting management in its analysis and pursuit of prudent organic cash flow growth strategies;
•Identifying and working with management to execute attractive external growth and acquisition opportunities; and
•Forming strong subsidiary-level boards of directors, including independent directors, to supplement management in developing and implementing strategic goals and objectives.

Our management team leverages a network of intermediaries, advisors, and other sources of opportunities who expose us to potential acquisitions. Through these relationships, we regularly evaluate a range of potential acquisition opportunities. Our management team also has experience navigating complex acquisition situations, including corporate spin-offs, family-owned business transitions, management buy-outs, and reorganizations. We believe this flexibility, creativity, experience and expertise in structuring transactions provides a strategic advantage to us in executing non-traditional and complex transactions tailored to fit a specific acquisition target.

previously issued financial statements for fiscal years 2022, 2023, 2024, and the first three fiscal quarters of 2025 including other interim and full-year financial information should no longer be relied upon. The Company corrected these errors in its 2024 Form 10-K/A which was filed on December 8, 2025, and its Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q for the first, second, and third quarters of 2025, which were filed on December 18, 2025, December 29, 2025 and January 14, 2026 respectively. The financial information discussed herein reflects the correction of these errors.

paragraphs: Compass Diversified Holdings，一家特拉華州法定信託，於2005年11月18日在特拉華州成立。Compass Group Diversified Holdings，LLC，一家特拉華州有限責任公司，亦於2005年11月18日成立。該信託與LLC成立的目的是取得並管理一羣總部位於北美地區的中小型及中型市場企業。該信託為LLC的Trust Interests（如LLC協議所定義）的100%所有者。根據LLC協議，該信託擁有與該信託現有股份數量相同的Trust Interests於LLC。
該信託先前在美國聯邦所得稅用途上被視為合夥企業，但自2021年9月1日起，選擇被課稅為一家可作為公司課稅的協會。
LLC為運營實體，設有董事會（"董事會"），其企業治理責任與特拉華州公司相似。LLC的董事會監督本公司及我們的業務與我們的經理的管理表現。某些為員工、前員工或我們經理成員的人士，透過Sostratus LLC作為受益所有人，獲得其業務的利潤分配（Allocation Interests），如LLC協議所定義。
我們取得並積極管理我們的子公司控制權，我們認為這些子公司（i）所處產業具有長期總體經濟成長機會，（ii）具有正面且穩定的現金流，（iii）面對極少的技術或競爭性過時威脅，（iv）擁有強大的管理團隊。我們為投資者提供獨特的機會，使其擁有北美地區品牌消費與工業領域中型市場領先企業的多樣組合。
我們對目標市場的嚴謹作法，提供了系統性取得並管理具吸引力企業的機會，這些企業將為我們股東創造價值。對企業所有者而言，我們獨特的財務結構使我們能以較少第三方融資條件，高效取得企業，並在取得後為企業提供成長資金。此外，我們的永久資本模式通常使我們能在經濟週期的任何階段取得企業，確保我們能在機會出現時迅速行動，即使市場波動。
私人企業經營者與希望出售其業務單位的母公司可能會認為我們是具有吸引力的買家，因為我們具備以下能力：
•為其業務提供持續的戰略與財務支援，包括在規模上專業化我們的子公司；
•對這些業務的所有權持有長期觀點；•在適當情況下，可持續投資於成長資金及/或附加收購；以及
•能有效完成交易，且不依賴第三方交易融資。
特別是，我們的長期策略與積極管理，可能緩解許多私人公司經營者與母公司對於其業務在短時間內經歷多次出售程序的擔憂。我們認為，我們的策略能提升我們發展全面戰略的能力，以增加各項業務的獲利與現金流。
最後，根據我們的經驗，我們在不需面對第三方交易融資常見的繁瑣延宕與條件的情況下，取得企業的能力，對重視機密性、速度與交易確定性的企業賣方而言具有吸引力。
我們管理團隊與產業主管、會計師、律師、企業經紀人、商業與投資銀行及其他潛在收購機會來源之間的強大關係，為我們提供評估可供收購的小至中型企業的機會。此外，我們管理團隊在交易結構上的靈活性、創造力、經驗與專業知識，使我們能考慮非傳統且複雜的交易，以符合特定收購目標的需要。
我們將目前所擁有的企業分為兩大類：(i) 品牌消費企業，以及 (ii) 工業企業。品牌消費企業是指我們認為能藉由其所在市場領域的寶貴品牌名稱來獲取競爭優勢的企業。我們認為，我們的品牌消費企業在其產品類別中為領導者。工業企業是指專注於製造與銷售產品及/或工業服務的企業，其業務範疇限定於特定市場領域。我們認為，我們的工業企業在其特定市場領域中為領導者。

paragraphs: 本項第 7 項包含前瞻性聲明。本年度 10-K 報告中之前瞻性聲明受多種風險與不確定性影響，其中一些風險與不確定性超出本公司控制範圍。本公司實際之結果、表現、前景或機會可能與前瞻性聲明中所表達或暗示者有重大差異。尚有其他風險，本公司目前尚未知悉或認為不重要，也可能導致本公司實際結果與預期有所差異，包括在本年度報告其他部分所載之 "前瞻性聲明" 與 "風險因素" 章節中所討論之風險。

Compass Diversified Holdings 為一設立於特拉華州之法定信託，於 2005 年 11 月 18 日成立。Compass Group Diversified Holdings LLC 為一設立於特拉華州之有限責任公司，亦於 2005 年 11 月 18 日成立。根據信託契約，信託為持有 100% 信託權益（如 LLC 契約中所定義）之唯一所有者。根據 LLC 契約，本公司持有與信託發行在外之股份數量相同之信託權益。Sostratus LLC 持有本公司全部之分配權益。本公司為營運實體，具有董事會與公司治理責任，與特拉華州公司相似。
信託與 LLC 成立之目的為取得並管理一羣設立於北美之中小型企業。我們將中小型企業定義為年現金流量達至 1 億美元之企業。我們專注於此規模之企業，因為我們認為此類企業較能實現高於相關產業之成長率，且改善獲利與現金流量之努力在該類企業中往往更具成效。在追求新進購併時，我們尋求具備以下特徵之企業：
• 設立於北美之營運基地； • 穩定且持續成長之獲利與現金流量； • 在具防禦性產業細分市場中擁有顯著市佔率（即，具有 "存在理由"）；
• 有實質激勵措施之穩健且經過驗證之管理團隊； • 低技術與/或產品過時風險；以及
• 多元化之客戶與供應商基礎。
本公司管理團隊對其子公司之策略為：
• 利用為每家公司量身打造之結構化激勵薪酬制度，以吸引並留住優秀管理人才；
•協助管理階層進行分析與追蹤謹慎的內生現金流成長策略;
•識別並與管理階層合作執行具吸引力的外部成長與收購機會; 和
•建立強固的子公司層級董事會，包括獨立董事，以輔助管理階層發展與執行戰略目標與計畫。
我們的管理團隊運用中介機構、顧問及其他機會來源的網路，使我們接觸到潛在的收購目標。透過這些關係，我們定期評估一系列潛在的收購機會。我們的管理團隊也具備處理複雜收購情境的經驗，包括公司分拆、家族企業過渡、管理階層收購及重整。我們相信這種靈活性、創造力、經驗與專業知識在結構交易方面，為我們執行非傳統且複雜的交易，並針對特定收購目標進行調整，提供了戰略優勢。

如前所披露，根據向本公司管理階層報告的關注事項，本公司啟動了 Lugano 調查。根據 Lugano 調查的結果，本公司決定，本公司 previously issued 的 2022 財年、2023 財年、2024 財年以及 2025 財年前三季的財務報表，以及其他間接與年度財務資訊，已不再可供依賴。本公司已在 2024 年 Form 10-K/A 中修正這些錯誤，該文件於 2025 年 12 月 8 日提交。本公司亦在 2025 年第一、第二及第三季度的季度報告 Form 10-Q 中修正這些錯誤，這些報告分別於 2025 年 12 月 18 日、2025 年 12 月 29 日及 2026 年 1 月 14 日提交。本文所討論的財務資訊已反映這些錯誤的修正。

本公司 previously issued 的 2022 財年、2023 財年、2024 財年以及 2025 財年前三季的財務報表，以及其他間接與年度財務資訊，已不再可供依賴。本公司已在 2024 年 Form 10-K/A 中修正這些錯誤，該文件於 2025 年 12 月 8 日提交。本公司亦在 2025 年第一、第二及第三季度的季度報告 Form 10-Q 中修正這些錯誤，這些報告分別於 2025 年 12 月 18 日、2025 年 12 月 29 日及 2026 年 1 月 14 日提交。本文所討論的財務資訊已反映這些錯誤的修正。

headings: 風險因素與 Lugano 調查及財務資料重述有關
本公司對 Lugano 的內部貸款存在損失風險。
本公司正面臨與 Lugano 事宜有關的政府調查，且該調查可能導致執行處分、處罰及額外成本。
與本公司業務及結構相關的風險
本公司自有品牌消費業務的成功取決於本公司維持品牌價值與聲譽的能力，若無法做到，可能減少利潤並對本公司財務狀況造成不利影響。
根據信託協議，本公司董事會有權在本公司股東可能不同意的情況下，單方面決定將信託轉為公司形式。
本公司完全依賴業務所得金額以支付股東分紅。
本公司董事會有權在本公司股東可能不同意的情況下，單方面改變本公司股份的條款。
本公司可能與我們業務之非控股股東產生利益衝突。
本公司負擔重大債務及對變動利率之敞口，可能嚴重影響本公司之流動性、財務狀況及經營業務之能力，以及償還債務及發放分紅之能力。
本公司可能與一個或多個目標企業進行業務交易，而該目標企業與本公司之董事長、董事或經理人有關係，可能產生利益衝突之潛在風險。
美國關稅及進出口規範之變更可能對經濟活動、財務狀況及本公司業務之結果產生負面影響。
與稅務相關之風險
未來稅法之變更具有不確定性，可能導致信託支付公司所得稅之稅率高於預期，或導致信託無法實現選項之預期效益。
與優先股相關之風險
系列 A 優先股之分紅為酌情發放且非累積性。
Series A、Series B 與 Series C 優先股為權益證券，且優先於本公司現有及未來的負債。
與我們管理人相關之風險
本公司管理人及其關係企業，包括本公司管理團隊成員，可能從事與我們或我們業務競爭之活動。
我們無法僅因表現不佳而解除管理人，此情形可能限制我們改善表現之能力，並可能對本公司股票之市場價格造成重大不利影響。
我們必須支付管理人基本管理費，與本公司表現無關。
我們無法確定隨時間推移將支付多少利潤分配金額。
本公司之利潤分配可能誘使管理人做出對本公司營運不利之決策。
支付管理費及利潤分配之義務可能導致本公司處分資產或負債。
與我們子公司相關的風險
與 Arnold 相關的風險
Arnold 的營運及其前身公司的過去營運，使其面臨重大環境責任的風險，這可能會對其財務狀況或營運成果產生負面影響。
與 Sterno 相關的風險
Sterno 的產品運作於高溫環境，並使用易燃燃料，這些因素均可能使我們的業務面臨產品責任索賠，這可能會損害其聲譽並減少客戶
與 Velocity Outdoor 相關的風險
Velocity 的產品可能涉及產品安全及責任訴訟，這可能會對其財務狀況、業務及營運成果產生重大負面影響。
一般風險因素
paragraphs: 本公司之業務、營運及財務狀況均面臨多種風險與不確定性。以下風險因素之說明應與本 10-K 表單第二部分第 7 項「管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之討論與分析」及「合併財務報表」與相關附註一併閱讀。若任何上述風險實際發生，將可能對本公司之業務、財務狀況、營運結果與前景造成重大且不利之影響。除影響本公司特定營運分部之因素外，以下討論列舉本公司所面臨之重大風險因素，這些因素使投資本公司之行為具有投機性或風險性。
因 Lugano 調查，本公司已重新調整部分先前之合併財務報表，此調查導致未預期之成本、對 Lugano 及本公司之訴訟，以及股東對本公司之訴訟，並可能導致更多股東訴訟、監管後果及我們目前尚未知悉之額外責任，並可能對投資人信心、本公司股票價格、未來籌資能力及本公司聲譽造成不利影響。

如前所述，因公司管理層接獲有關報告，本公司啟動 Lugano 調查。因 Lugano 調查，本公司決定先前發佈之 2022 財年、2023 財年、2024 財年及 2025 財年前三季之財務報表，以及其他臨時及全年財務資訊，已無法依賴。本公司於 2025 年 12 月 8 日提交之 2024 年 10-K/A 表單，以及 2025 年第一、第二、第三季之季報（10-Q 表單），分別於 2025 年 12 月 18 日、2025 年 12 月 29 日及 2026 年 1 月 14 日提交，已修正這些錯誤。

本公司因 Lugano 調查及財務報表修正，已產生未預期之會計、融資及法律費用，包括因潛在違約或違約事件而與信用協議及高階債券契約簽訂緩衝協議、修正條款及豁免條款所產生之費用。財務報表修正可能削弱投資人對本公司之信心、財務報導、會計作業與流程，並可能對本公司業務造成聲譽問題。Lugano 調查及財務報表修正已對本公司證券之交易價格造成負面影響，並使本公司更難符合債務契約之條件，緊縮流動性，並可能使本公司未來更難以可接受之條件或完全無法籌資。因 Lugano 調查及相關事項，本公司已採取若干行動以維持流動性，包括暫停普通股之分紅，且因 Lugano 調查及相關事件，本公司於 2025 年在 equity capital markets 進行 at-the-market 股權發行之能力受到限制。

此外，Lugano 調查、財務報表修正及本公司財務報導內部控制之重大弱點，已導致對 Lugano 及本公司之訴訟，以及對本公司之股東訴訟，以及監管機構之調查與詢問，可能導致不利之監管後果。如前所述，美國證券交易委員會（SEC）及美國司法部（DOJ）已啟動持續調查，且 FINRA 對本公司證券之交易活動進行審查，並將該事項轉交 SEC 以進行 SEC 認為適當之行動，如有。這些及未來任何監管後果、訴訟、聲請或爭議，無論是否成功，均可能使本公司面臨額外成本或責任，分散本公司管理層之注意力，或損害本公司聲譽。上述任何後果均可能對本公司之業務、營運結果及財務狀況造成重大不利影響。

本公司已識別出財務報導內部控制之重大弱點，若未妥善解決，可能導致本公司中期或年度合併財務報表出現額外重大錯誤，影響本公司準確且及時報導營運結果與財務狀況之能力。若本公司無法解決這些重大弱點，或未來識別出更多重大弱點，或未能維持財務報導內部控制有效性或揭露控制與程序，可能導致本公司合併財務報表出現未來重大錯誤，或使本公司無法履行定期報導義務，這可能對本公司之業務、財務狀況、營運結果、投資人對本公司業務之信心，或本公司證券之交易價格造成不利影響。
